items.stem: Which feature protects objects from being permanently lost when they are overwritten or deleted?

options.rationale: Correct: versioning retains previous versions of an object.
Instance type is unrelated to S3 object protection.
Encryption is about confidentiality, not recovery from deletion.
Security groups apply to network traffic, not S3 objects.

items.explanation: Correct: versioning retains previous versions of an object.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices for securing an S3 bucket? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep Block Public Access enabled unless public access is explicitly required
options.rationale: Correct: Block Public Access prevents accidental exposure.

options.text: Grant access with a least-privilege bucket policy or IAM
options.rationale: Correct: least-privilege limits who can access objects.

options.text: Make the bucket public for convenience
Share root account keys with applications
options.rationale: Root keys are insecure and over-privileged.

items.explanation: Correct: Block Public Access and least-privilege policies secure a bucket.

items.stem: Data is written once and rarely read again after 30 days. Which approach optimizes cost?

options.text: A lifecycle rule that transitions objects to a colder, cheaper storage class
options.rationale: Correct: lifecycle rules move aging data to lower-cost tiers automatically.

options.text: Keep everything in S3 Standard forever
options.rationale: Standard is more expensive for rarely accessed data.

options.text: Delete the data immediately to save cost
options.rationale: Deleting needed data is not an optimization.

options.text: Move the data to an EC2 instance store
options.rationale: Instance store is ephemeral and unsuitable for retention.

items.explanation: Correct: lifecycle rules move aging data to lower-cost tiers automatically.
